text: You already use a coding agent. It's sharp for an hour. Then the session ends, and what it learned goes with it.
Keelson is the harness that sits under that agent. One small server, on your own machine. No hosted service, and nothing to sign in to.
It starts with chat. You talk to your agent through Keelson, in the browser or the terminal.
And it keeps the state. Conversations, runs, and the memories you approve are saved locally, and your secrets stay in the keychain.
It makes work repeatable. A workflow is a small YAML graph of agent steps, shell steps, and approval gates, run in the same order every time.
ssml: It makes work repeatable. A workflow is a small <sub alias="yammel">YAML</sub> graph of agent steps, shell steps, and approval gates, run in the same order every time.

text: It doesn't tie you to one model. Claude, Copilot, Codex, or Pi, chosen per chat, or per step.
ssml: It doesn't tie you to one model. Claude, Co Pilot, Codex, or Pi, chosen per chat, or per step.

text: There are three ways in. The browser, the keelson command line for your shell and scripts, and MCP, so the agent you already use can drive it too.
ssml: There are three ways in. The browser, the Keelson command line for your shell and scripts, and MCP, so the agent you already use can drive it too.

text: Over MCP, you decide how much it can do. Read only, or full control, with a token when you want one.
That's the keel, and it's useful on its own.
When you need more, you raise ribs. A rib is a package that adds tools, workflows, and whole new screens, without forking the harness.
One backbone, many ribs. Every other figure in this series builds on this frame.
Keelson. Lay the keel, raise the ribs.
